idiom_name: scala.ref.WeakReference (Option-returning get plus extractor) over java.lang.ref; scala.collection.mutable.WeakHashMap
implementation_notes: Scala wraps the JVM facility instead of inventing one: scala.ref.WeakReference wraps java.lang.ref.WeakReference, returns Option[T] from get (Some while the referent lives, None once collected) and ships a companion extractor so a weak value can be pattern-matched - which turns the promotion step into ordinary Option handling. For weak-keyed maps, scala.collection.mutable.WeakHashMap wraps java.util.WeakHashMap and removes entries when a key is no longer strongly referenced. The semantics underneath remain the JVM's: clearing and queueing are the collector's decisions, and a long-lived WeakReference keeps the weak count, not the object, alive.
pitfalls: get returns Option[T]: promote once with a match, .map or .flatMap and never hold an Option across collection points expecting it to stay Some.
WeakHashMap wraps java.util.WeakHashMap, so keys are compared with equals/hashCode rather than identity, the map can shrink at any time, and a value that strongly refers to its key pins the entry.
scala.ref.WeakReference is JVM-only, so Scala.js and Scala Native code cannot use it through these classes - the platform has no weak-reference facility exposed there.
